summary: Contribution candidate exists but no external credit observed.

sections.summary: 2 of 3 contribution candidate(s) met the credit-eligibility threshold in Phase 11.
sections.detail: Dan-Go Phase 11 recorded contribution events as candidates. 2 candidate(s) have candidate_credit=true, meaning they completed accepted work (evidence_reviewed, evidence_accepted, reaffirm_submitted, or plan_correction). This is an advisory classification — it does not trigger any action.

sections.summary: No external credit observed in gitsea.
sections.detail: Dan-Go observed gitsea and found no credit record corresponding to the contribution candidates above. This is not an error. External credit systems are sovereign — gitsea decides independently whether and when to issue credit. Dan-Go does not request, push, or activate credit.

sections.summary: The gap between candidate credit and external credit is not a protocol contradiction.
sections.detail: Dan-Go candidate credit and external credit are different things. A candidate existing in Dan-Go does not mean external credit was issued or is owed. A gap between the two states is expected and by design. External credit systems such as GITSEA are sovereign: they may issue credit at any time, on their own schedule, or not at all. Dan-Go does not guarantee credit. Dan-Go records candidates.

sections.summary: Dan-Go's role ends at observation. Making contribution legible is the goal — not issuing credit.
sections.detail: The Dan-Go protocol is designed to make contribution legible before it becomes economically valuable. Recording candidates, building contribution history, and surfacing them for external system observation is the complete role of Dan-Go in the credit process. Whether value follows is determined by external systems. Observation is not issuance. Dan-Go has fulfilled its role by recording candidates accurately and making them observable.

principle_2: Candidate credit is not external credit.
principle_3: Contribution becomes legible before it becomes valuable.
